caption: What if you lived on Venus? It's nearly the same size as Earth and comes closer to us than any other planet. Step outside and the ground is about 465 °C, hot enough to melt lead. The air presses down about 92 times harder than on Earth, like standing 1 km under the sea. The clouds are made of sulfuric acid, and the toughest lander ever sent, the Soviet Venera 13, lasted just 127 minutes in 1982. Venus also spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west. One spin takes about 243 Earth days, but one trip around the Sun takes only 225, so a day there is longer than a year. India's Shukrayaan orbiter is planned to launch in 2028. Plot twist: about 50 km up, the pressure is close to Earth's, temperatures sit between 0 and 50 °C, and plain breathable air is lighter than the CO2 around it, so a home full of air would float like a balloon. Would YOU live in the clouds of Venus? 👇
